mechanism: Inhibition of methotrexate renal tubular secretion
effect: Methotrexate toxicity — bone marrow suppression, nephrotoxicity
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative antibiotic. Monitor FBC and renal function.

mechanism: Chelation in GI tract reduces ciprofloxacin absorption
management: Separate doses by at least 2 hours (ciprofloxacin first).

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases statin plasma levels
management: Temporarily suspend statin therapy during macrolide course. Use azithromycin if possible.

mechanism: Serotonin syndrome via additive serotonergic effect
effect: Serotonin syndrome — agitation, hyperthermia, tachycardia, seizures
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative analgesic. If combined, monitor closely for serotonin syndrome symptoms.

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and CYP enzyme metabolism of digoxin
effect: Digoxin toxicity — nausea, arrhythmia, visual disturbances
management: Reduce digoxin dose by 50%. Monitor serum digoxin levels and ECG.
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for 48 hours after completing metronidazole.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition by amlodipine increases simvastatin exposure
management: Limit simvastatin dose to 20mg/day. Consider switching to rosuvastatin or pravastatin.
Avoid combination. If necessary, use lowest effective doses with close monitoring and naloxone available.

mechanism: Probenecid blocks renal tubular secretion of penicillin
management: Can be used intentionally to prolong penicillin effect (e.g., gonorrhoea treatment). Monitor for toxicity.

management: Avoid combination. Use artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) per NHMIS guidelines.
